test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Rose painted the most beautifulest picture ever at the art class today!
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the use of the double superlative "**most beautifulest**."
 
• Superlatives are used to indicate the highest degree of a quality, and typically, only one form (either "most" + adjective or adjective + "-est") should be used.
 
• The correct phrasing would be either "**the most beautiful**" or, less commonly for longer adjectives, "**the beautifulest**" (though the former is preferred).
 
• Therefore, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Rose painted **the most beautiful** picture ever at the art class today!"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1) Rose painted** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not contain the error.
 
• **2) picture ever at the** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not contain the error.
 
• **4) art class today!** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not contain the error.
 
• Using double superlatives like "most beautifulest" is a common grammatical mistake. It's important to use either the "most + adjective" form or the "adjective + -est" form, but not both together.
